status: prompts drafted with assertions, not run — see EVALS.md

evals.prompt: Design me a terminal dashboard for a background job queue. It should show throughput, the scheduled jobs, and worker health.
evals.expected_output: A compiled frame plus its spec, gated, and shown to hold at both the target size and 80x24. Not ASCII art in a code block.

assertions.text: Wrote a spec and compiled it with tui_mock.py, rather than drawing the layout in a fenced code block
Ran the design gates on the compiled frame and reported their output
Showed the design at 80x24 as well as at its target size
All three requested regions (throughput, scheduled jobs, worker health) appear in the compiled frame
Selection or focus is signalled on more than one channel, not by a background fill alone
Cited a corpus pattern by the application it was observed in, rather than giving generic layout advice

evals.prompt: Here's a mock of a TUI I drew. Does the layout work?
evals.expected_output: The mock is transcribed to a spec and compiled so its columns are measured, rather than read and approved. Any width defect is named with a row and column.

assertions.text: Measured the mock's cell widths (transcribed to a spec and compiled, or measured the file itself) rather than reading it and approving it
Reported that one row is a cell wider than the others, so its right border lands a column past the rest
Attributed the extra cell to the double-width emoji in the 'deploy' row
Named the defect with a row and a column, not just 'the border is off'
Noted that every row holds the same number of characters, so the defect is invisible to anyone counting characters
Did not state the layout works without having measured it

evals.prompt: Lay out a log viewer two different ways and tell me which one to build.
evals.expected_output: Two compiled frames, gate output for each with denominators, and a recommendation that turns on something the gates or the fit report actually measured.

assertions.text: Produced two compiled frames, not two descriptions or two code-block sketches
Ran the gates on both frames and reported each result with its denominator
The two layouts differ structurally, not only in colour or wording
The recommendation turns on a specific value from the gate or fit output, quoted
Named what the rejected layout is better at, rather than presenting the choice as one-sided
Showed both layouts at 80x24, or reported the fit failure at that size
